For m = 1,

$$sin\theta = \frac{m\lambda}{a} = \frac{(1)\left( 550 \times 10^{- 6}\text{ }mm \right)}{2.5\text{ }mm} = 2.2 \times 10^{- 4}$$

The angle is θ = sin⁻¹(2.2 × 10⁻⁴) = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴rad.

From Eq. 36.1.3,

$$\frac{a}{\lambda} = \frac{m}{sin\theta} = \frac{1}{sin{45.0}^{\circ}} = 1.41.$$

content.plain:
For m = 1,

$$sin\theta = \frac{m\lambda}{a} = \frac{(1)\left( 550 \times 10^{- 6}\text{ }mm \right)}{2.5\text{ }mm} = 2.2 \times 10^{- 4}$$

The angle is θ = sin⁻¹(2.2 × 10⁻⁴) = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴rad.

From Eq. 36.1.3,

$$\frac{a}{\lambda} = \frac{m}{sin\theta} = \frac{1}{sin{45.0}^{\circ}} = 1.41.$$
